省.meaning: A stingy one-eyed pirate glares with his single bloodshot <part>eye</part> at his candle and lets it burn for only a <part>few</part> seconds a night, then counts his coins in the dark. He even rations his parrot to a few words a week. 'Waste nothing,' he growls. He lives to <kanji>conserve</kanji>.
省.on: He even turns off the lights in the middle of a <sound>show</sound> to save power.
省.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' he snorts, and trims his <sound>bu</sound>shy beard by half: less to wash.

深.meaning: A fisherman ties his <part>net</part> to the top of a tall <part>tree</part> and lowers it into a dark lake, <part>water drops</part> dripping off every branch. Down, down, the whole tree slides in after it and still doesn't touch the bottom. That lake is very <kanji>deep</kanji>.
深.on: He leans over to look and bangs his <sound>shin</sound> on the edge of the jetty.
深.kun: He gives up and floats on a <sound>fu</sound>ton, while a <sound>ca</sound>rp swims down to look for his tree.

構.meaning: A <part>tree</part> wants to look its best for a painter, so it leans on some <part>scaffolding</part>: chest out, branches back, chin up. It holds the pose for nine hours without a wobble. The painter calls it perfect <kanji>posture</kanji>.
構.on: A squirrel on the scaffold licks an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne the whole time.
構.kun: The painter's <sound>ca</sound>lm <sound>ma</sound>ma holds the easel steady and takes her stance beside it.

破.meaning: A caveman stretches a bear <part>pelt</part> over a big <part>stone</part> to make a cosy seat. He pulls one corner, then the other, harder, harder: rrrip! It splits right down the middle. He's managed to <kanji>rend</kanji> it in two.
破.on: Now he has only half a rug for the floor of his <sound>hu</sound>t.
破.kun: He drags the torn halves out into the <sound>ya</sound>rd and hangs them on a <sound>bu</sound>sh.

補.meaning: A farmer's <part>weathervane</part> loses one arm in a storm, so he tapes a <part>flyswatter</part> to the stump. Now it spins again, and swats flies as it turns. It's not the real thing, but it's a handy <kanji>supplement</kanji>.
補.on: A fly lands on the farmer's <sound>ho</sound>tdog, and whap!
補.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' honk the <sound>gee</sound>se, as it swats a fly off their <sound>na</sound>an.

認.meaning: A shy knight has to <part>endure</part> a long <part>speech</part> from a dragon, listing every village it has ever burnt. At the end the dragon sniffs, 'Fine. You did beat me.' The knight finally gets the nod he wanted: the dragon has to <kanji>acknowledge</kanji> him.
認.on: A <sound>nin</sound>ja hidden in the rafters writes it all down as proof.
認.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>?' squeaks the knight, standing on <sound>to</sound>p of the rubble.
